مُتَآزِفٌ , of the measure مُتَفَاعِلٌ, applied to a man, (TA,) Short; (S, A, K;) as being contracted in make; (A, TA;) having his several parts near together. (S, K.) [In the CK it is written مُتَأزِّف, in this sense and others, following.] ―
-b2- A strait, or narrow, place. (O, L, K.) ―
-b3- A contracted stepping: you say, خَطْوٌ مُتَآزِفٌ: so in the O and L. (TA.) ―
-b4- (tropical:) A man (Sgh, TA) evil in disposition; narrow-minded: (Sgh, K, TA:) weak; cowardly. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
